title: Wall Street Week | Soft US Jobs, Swedish Defense Spending, Private Credit Woes
content:
This week, Steven Rattner of Willett Advisors explains why the US labor market is softening and what tariffs, AI and stagflation risk could mean next. And as Europe prepares to spend more on defense, Sweden is emerging as an unlikely but crucial player in the continent’s push. Plus, private credit’s advantages are becoming vulnerabilities as some investors try to get their money out. Later, Nepal’s Gen Z protests toppled a government, and now the country’s voters are trying to turn that uprising into lasting change.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Economic Outlook Dragged Down by Iran War | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/13/2026
content: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Bloomberg's Mike McKee about the fed's preferred inflation gauge and the economic impact of the Iran war on the US economy. Then, Mike Collins, managing director at PGIM Fixed Income, on the state of the bond market and the current private credit landscape. Plus, Kyivstar Group president and CEO Oleksandr Komarov joins the show from Kyiv to talk earnings from Ukraine's largest telecommunications company and providing services to a country at war. Finally, Bloomberg's Katrina Manson breaks down how the US military enlisted silicon valley to build up its AI warfare. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Economy Loses Steam, Adobe CEO Exits After 18 Years
content:
Get a jump start on the US trading day with Matt Miller and Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest."
Iran’s Supreme Leader reportedly wounded, as President Trump issues a stark new warning to Tehran. Bank of America’s Michael Hartnett says markets are flashing 2008-style signals, with oil near triple digits and private credit risks rising. And a wave of fresh data shows the US  economy losing steam, with consumers pulling back and inflation pressures building. And Adobe's CEO is stepping down in the face of investor concerns over AI.
Plus — Burlington’s CEO on why off-price retail is poised to win now, Goodwill’s CEO on closing America’s labor and AI skills gap, and inside a $5 million Ferrari trade as rare supercars become a red-hot asset class. (Source: Bloomberg)
